title: FlowTrace: CLI and Neovim plugin code paths

overview.label: FlowTrace has two runtimes: a Go CLI and a Neovim Lua plugin
overview.summary: The CLI builds/validates/prints .flow.json artifacts. The Neovim plugin loads one and renders an interactive tree you can jump from. The two share only the .flow.json file format (defined in schema.go).

cli-main.label: CLI entrypoint: main() reads os.Args and dispatches
cli-main.summary: Tiny entrypoint. Requires at least one arg, then a switch on os.Args[1] picks the subcommand. Errors bubble up and exit non-zero.

cli-dispatch.label: Subcommand switch: build / context / validate / print
cli-dispatch.summary: Four real commands plus help. Each runX function parses its own flag.NewFlagSet and then calls into the core package.

cli-build-cmd.label: runBuild parses flags and calls core.Build
cli-build-cmd.summary: Reads --root, --out, --max-files, --max-nodes, --dry-run plus the request string, then hands BuildOptions to core.Build.

cli-context-cmd.label: runContext is just core.Build with DryRun=true
cli-context-cmd.summary: Same code path as build, but DryRun=true short-circuits before any artifact is written. Used to dump candidate snippets for an agent to read.

cli-validate-cmd.label: runValidate loads a .flow.json and validates it
cli-validate-cmd.summary: Two steps only: core.LoadFlow then core.ValidateFlow against --root.

cli-print-cmd.label: runPrint loads a .flow.json and renders the tree to stdout
cli-print-cmd.summary: core.LoadFlow then core.PrintFlow(os.Stdout, flow). No validation; just walks and prints.

core-build.label: core.Build orchestrates: search → scaffold → normalize → validate → write
core-build.summary: Heart of the build pipeline. Tokenizes the request, walks the repo for candidate hits, formats snippets (and exits if DryRun), otherwise builds a heuristic Flow, normalizes it, validates it, and writes the JSON.

request-terms.label: requestTerms tokenizes the natural-language request
request-terms.summary: Lowercases, splits on word chars, drops a small stopword set and tokens shorter than 3 chars. Returns a deduped slice used by searchRepo.

search-repo.label: searchRepo walks the repo and scores candidate files
search-repo.anchor: func searchRepo(root string, terms []string, max int)
search-repo.summary: filepath.WalkDir, skipping .git/.flowtrace/node_modules/vendor/dist/build/target. For each text-source file: +1 per matching line (stores up to 8), +3 per term that hits the relative path. Sorts by score desc and trims to max.

format-snippets.label: formatSnippets prints `## file (score N)` blocks for the agent
format-snippets.summary: Markdown-ish dump of each candidate file plus its matched lines. This is the entire output of the `context` subcommand.

heuristic-flow.label: heuristicFlow scaffolds a linear Flow from the top candidates
heuristic-flow.summary: Greedy: each candidate becomes one node-N FlowNode in score order, chained as parent→child. Resolution is set to `search`. Fallback emits a single placeholder pointing at README.md if no candidates matched.

normalize.label: normalizeAndResolve fixes paths, defaults, and stale refs
normalize.summary: Cleans file paths, defaults Column to 1, defaults Resolution to llm_inferred, and if a node's file doesn't exist it tries to remap by basename to a known candidate.

validate-flow.label: ValidateFlow checks schema, files, line numbers, child/branch refs
validate-flow.summary: Required fields, root node exists, each node id matches its map key, file exists under root and is not a dir, line is within the file, every child id and branch target id exists, resolution is one of: lsp/ast/search/llm_inferred/llm_validated/manual.

count-lines.label: countLines reads the file and counts newlines
count-lines.summary: Used by ValidateFlow to make sure node.Line never exceeds the file length.

write-flow.label: WriteFlow marshals indented JSON and writes the artifact
write-flow.summary: json.MarshalIndent with two-space indent plus trailing newline. The output path defaults to `.flowtrace/<slug>.flow.json` if --out is empty.

load-flow.label: LoadFlow reads and json.Unmarshals into *Flow
load-flow.summary: Single source of truth for parsing. Both validate and print go through this.

print-flow.label: PrintFlow writes the title then recurses from the root
print-flow.summary: Maintains a `seen` map so cycles or shared subtrees print once and then say `↳ already shown`.

print-node.label: printNode draws └─/├─ tree connectors per node, then children, then branches
print-node.anchor: func printNode(w io.Writer, f *Flow, id, prefix string
print-node.summary: Recursive. Branches are rendered after children with a `branch:` label so they read as alternative paths in the tree.

nvim-plugin.label: Neovim plugin file: registers four :FlowTrace* user commands
nvim-plugin.summary: Loaded once per session via the `vim.g.loaded_flowtrace` guard. Each command is a thin wrapper that lazy-requires `flowtrace` and calls into init.lua.

cmd-open.label: :FlowTraceOpen → require('flowtrace').open(path)
cmd-open.summary: User command with file completion. Forwards the single arg to M.open.

cmd-last.label: :FlowTraceLast → opens the most recent .flowtrace/*.flow.json
cmd-last.summary: Convenience for re-opening whatever the agent just wrote.

cmd-refresh.label: :FlowTraceRefresh → re-parse current path and redraw
cmd-refresh.summary: Useful when the agent rewrites the artifact while the tree window is open.

cmd-close.label: :FlowTraceClose → close the tree window
cmd-close.summary: Closes state.win if it is still valid. The buffer is wipe-on-hidden so it disappears with the window.

nvim-open.label: M.open: load → side window → keys → first redraw
nvim-open.summary: Captures the current window as `state.source_win` (so jumps know where to land), parses the JSON, opens the side panel, wires keymaps, and draws the tree.

parser-load.label: parser.load reads the file and vim.json.decodes it
parser-load.summary: Validates that the decoded value has `nodes` (table) and `root`. Errors are raised, not returned.

window-open.label: window.open_buffer creates the left-side scratch buffer
window-open.summary: `topleft vertical Nnew` at ~42% width. Sets buftype=nofile, bufhidden=wipe, filetype=flowtrace, plus wrap/linebreak/cursorline.

nvim-setup-keys.label: setup_keys binds <CR>/p/?/o/q/r in the tree buffer
nvim-setup-keys.summary: Buffer-local normal-mode mappings. `o` flips state.expanded[id] and redraws; everything else delegates to actions.lua or M.close/M.refresh.

nvim-redraw.label: redraw renders lines + extmarks into the tree buffer
nvim-redraw.summary: Calls tree.render(flow, expanded), replaces buffer lines, clears the FlowTrace namespace, then re-applies highlights as extmarks. Buffer is flipped non-modifiable around the writes.

tree-render.label: tree.render builds the lines/index/highlights triple
tree-render.summary: Emits a title line, a help line, a blank line, then walks the flow starting at `flow.root`. `index` maps buffer line → {id, node} so actions can resolve the node under the cursor.

tree-add-node.label: add_node recursively writes label + meta + file + summary lines
tree-add-node.summary: Per node: a `▾/▸` marker line for the label, an optional meta line (kind and source), a `file: path:line` line, and an optional summary line. Then recurses into children, then into branches (with a `↳ label:` prefix). A `seen` map prevents infinite recursion and prints `↳ already shown` instead.

nvim-last.label: M.last globs .flowtrace/*.flow.json and opens the last one
nvim-last.summary: table.sort puts the lexicographically last file at the end. With slugged filenames this is essentially "most recently named", not "most recently modified".

nvim-refresh.label: M.refresh re-parses state.path and redraws
nvim-refresh.summary: No-op if no path has been opened. Reuses the existing tree buffer/window and the current `state.expanded` map.

action-jump.label: actions.jump opens the node's file in a code window and lands the cursor
action-jump.summary: Picks a code window (or creates one), `:edit`s the file, resolves a line via anchor → symbol → node.line, sets the cursor, and centers with `zz`.

action-preview.label: actions.preview opens the file via :pedit in the preview window
action-preview.summary: Same code-window + resolve_location dance as jump, but opens the result with `:pedit +<line>` so the cursor stays in the FlowTrace tree.

action-details.label: actions.details opens a centered floating buffer with node metadata
action-details.summary: Builds a small markdown buffer (label, type, file:line, anchor, source, summary) and shows it as a rounded floating window. q or <Esc> closes it.

code-window.label: code_window picks (or creates) a non-FlowTrace window to jump into
code-window.summary: Tries `state.source_win` first, then any other window whose buffer isn't a sidebar/picker/help/qf. As a last resort splits a `rightbelow vertical new` so the tree stays put.

resolve-location.label: resolve_location matches anchor → symbol → falls back to node.line
resolve-location.summary: find_in_buffer first does a plain substring match on node.anchor, then a whitespace-tolerant regex retry, then repeats both with node.symbol. This is why anchors survive minor edits — the node.line is only the last-resort fallback.
